overview: Belgium is a small country in Western Europe on the North Sea. Its capital, Brussels, is home to the main institutions of the European Union and the headquarters of NATO. Belgium has three official languages: Dutch, spoken mainly in Flanders in the north; French, spoken mainly in Wallonia in the south; and German, in a small area in the east. It is known for chocolate, waffles and comic books.

geography.text: Northern Belgium is low and flat, with a short, sandy North Sea coast and farmland crossed by rivers and canals. The land rises towards the south-east into the forested hills of the Ardennes. The Scheldt and the Meuse are its main rivers, and the port of Antwerp on the Scheldt is one of the largest in Europe.

history.text: Belgium's land was fought over for centuries by Europe's great powers and ruled in turn by Spain, Austria, France and the Netherlands. It broke away from the Netherlands and became independent in 1830. Belgium was invaded in both World Wars, and after 1945 it became a founding member of what is now the European Union, with Brussels as its main home.

events.title: Battle of Waterloo
events.text: Napoleon is finally defeated just south of Brussels.

events.title: Belgian Revolution
events.text: Belgium breaks away from the Netherlands and becomes independent.

events.title: Congo Free State
events.text: King Leopold II takes the Congo as his personal colony, where millions suffer under forced labour.

events.title: German invasion
events.text: Germany invades neutral Belgium at the start of the First World War.

events.title: Founding member of the EEC
events.text: Belgium helps found the European Economic Community, which becomes the EU.

government.text: Belgium is a constitutional monarchy with a king as head of state and a Prime Minister leading the government. It is a federal state split into regions and language communities: Dutch-speaking Flanders, French-speaking Wallonia, bilingual Brussels and a small German-speaking area. Forming a government can take a long time; in 2010–11 it took 541 days.

economy.text: Belgium sits at the heart of Europe's trade routes. The port of Antwerp is one of Europe's largest, and the country is strong in chemicals, medicines, diamonds and food products. Brussels is home to the main institutions of the European Union and the headquarters of NATO.

culture.text: Belgium is famous for chocolate, waffles, beer and fries, which Belgians insist they invented. It is a powerhouse of comics: Tintin and the Smurfs are Belgian. Painters from the region include Jan van Eyck, Pieter Bruegel and the surrealist René Magritte.

items.title: Tintin
items.text: Hergé's young reporter first appeared in 1929 and has been translated into more than 100 languages.

items.title: Belgian beer culture
items.text: Listed by UNESCO as intangible heritage in 2016.

items.title: Grand-Place
items.text: The ornate main square of Brussels.

sport.text: Cycling is a passion in Belgium, which has produced great riders such as Eddy Merckx, who won the Tour de France five times. Football is also hugely popular; the national team, nicknamed the Red Devils, finished third at the 2018 World Cup.

items.title: Eddy Merckx
items.text: Often called the greatest cyclist of all time.
Belgium finished third at the World Cup, its best ever result.

items.title: Spa-Francorchamps
items.text: A famous Formula 1 circuit in the Ardennes hills.

didYouKnow: Belgium has three official languages: Dutch, French and German.
The saxophone was invented by Adolphe Sax, a Belgian, in the 1840s.
